title: Certified Accounting for Adaptive Shuffled Gaussian Training
abstract: This preprint develops a certified privacy accountant for multi-epoch shuffled training with Gaussian noise, heterogeneous items, and queries that adapt to earlier releases. A null-clone reduction bounds likelihood sums by candidate count and produces a finite rational dominating pair that composes across epochs. For 1,000 batches per epoch, five epochs, noise multiplier 1, and delta = 10^-8, the paper brackets the worst-case epsilon of the full adaptive transcript in (6.423, 7.97], while matched Poisson sampling is certified at 0.507. It also gives an adaptive counterexample to the proposed dominating pair of Chua et al. The dominating-pair construction, counterexample, and supporting certificate lemmas are formalized in Lean 4; the paper identifies the reduction and other steps that remain in the written proofs.

title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities. We propose Product Monte Carlo (PMC), an algorithm for computing arbitrary expectations under a product of densities using only Monte Carlo draws from individual densities. We turn the intractable product expectation into a regression problem by expressing it through a family of computable conditional expectations. Besides the point estimate, our fully Bayesian regression formulation provides coherent uncertainty quantification and principled diagnostics. We establish theoretical guarantees on consistency and characterize convergence rates for the PMC estimator. Across simulated and real-data experiments varying the number, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of the component distributions, PMC achieves higher estimation accuracy, better-calibrated uncertainty coverage, and improved scalability at a lower computational cost than existing methods. In addition, PMC requires no density evaluation, making it applicable to simulation-based inference, as we demonstrate in an application with protein images.

title: Horizon symmetries of exact hydrodynamic actions
abstract: We demonstrate how horizon symmetries of AdS black holes are realised in the hydrodynamic actions for the dynamics of the dual stress tensor. A recent approach for obtaining such actions involves a choice of horizon boundary conditions, and we show that diffeomorphisms that preserve these give rise to symmetries of the corresponding hydrodynamic action. We obtain explicit hydrodynamic actions for small amplitude perturbations of black holes in JT and AdS_3 gravity using this approach and demonstrate explicitly the existence of these symmetries. For a natural choice of boundary conditions, the resulting actions manifestly realise gauge symmetries previously proposed for effective theories of maximal chaos.

title: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury
abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is prevalent among adolescents with depression, but the rapid brain-state dynamics linking social distress to maladaptive behavior remain unclear. We combine an experimental pain paradigm, electroencephalography (EEG) microstate analysis, and interpretable deep sequence modeling to investigate NSSI-related neurodynamics in 106 adolescents with depression, including 67 with NSSI (DN+) and 39 without NSSI (DN-), during social pain, physical pain, and resting-state conditions. A model integrating disease-specific, domain-adversarial, consistency, and contrastive learning captures higher-order dependencies in microstate sequences. Social pain yields the strongest NSSI discrimination, with 68.55% accuracy, outperforming the best baseline by 8.94% points. Model interpretation and conventional microstate analyses reveal weakened bidirectional transitions between MS3 and MS5 in DN+ adolescents during social pain. Source reconstruction associates MS3 with emotional/interoceptive processing and MS5 with action preparation, suggesting disrupted emotion-action coupling. Time-resolved analyses show greater early-to-middle action-state recruitment and later emotion-state recruitment in DN+ adolescents. In DN- adolescents, MS5-to-MS3 dynamics mediate associations between social-evaluation sensitivity and affective outcomes, whereas this mediation is absent in DN+; conversely, MS3-to-MS5 transitions are associated with greater negative affect in DN+. Together, these findings identify disrupted emotion-action coupling as a key neurodynamic mechanism underlying altered social pain processing in adolescents with NSSI, providing a mechanistically interpretable neural signature for objective identification of NSSI.

title: Fast thinnings via segment maps
authors: a N Ç O I S P O T T I E R, F, R
abstract: We present the segment map, a purely functional data structure that represents an increasing function of the natural numbers into the natural numbers, also known as a thinning. This data structure, a variant of Okasaki's skew binary random access lists, offers efficient support for many operations, including lookup, reverse lookup, horizontal and vertical displacements, insertion at the front end, and composition. We present a verified implementation and an analysis of its time complexity. This data structure may be useful in proof assistants, compilers, and symbolic computation systems where variables are encoded as de Bruijn indices or co-de Bruijn indices.

title: Large language model consensus for reliable research cohort construction from radiology reports: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Large-scale retrospective studies often require researchers to adjudicate outcomes or cohort eligibility from unstructured clinical records. Manual review can provide reliable labels but is difficult to scale. We developed and evaluated a consensus workflow using multiple large language models (LLMs) to automatically assign high-confidence outcome labels while deferring ambiguous cases for manual review. Methods We included 6,718 brain MRI reports from 5,856 patients. The expert-adjudicated reference set included 680 reports from 675 patients: 372 normal (age-appropriate without significant intracranial pathology), 90 white matter hyperintensity-only (WMH-only; isolated nonspecific WMHs potentially ambiguous for binary classification), and 218 abnormal (other intracranial pathology) reports. This strategy may reduce the burden of manual adjudication and support scalable construction of high-purity research cohorts from unstructured clinical text.

title: goalbench: a reproducible benchmark of choice-style deciders for customer-goal classification in Brazilian Portuguese
abstract: goalbench measures small "decider" models that answer typed choice questions (Laya, Strands Decider) on customer-goal classification in Brazilian Portuguese, inside a two-stage pipeline: an embedding shortlist of 10 goals followed by the decider, with a calibrated combination fitted by cross-validation. Runs log every phrase, control for option-order (position) bias, and report Wilson intervals and exact McNemar tests. A parallel English translation of the dataset measures the accuracy lost in Brazilian Portuguese and the gain from a language-specific checkpoint. The archive includes the code (Apache-2.0), the synthetic datasets (CC BY 4.0) and the raw per-phrase logs of every run reported in docs/results.md and docs/results-language.md.

title: On the security of TLS session tickets
abstract: TLS schützt den Großteil des Online-Datenverkehrs. Um die Leistung zu verbessern, ermöglicht TLS die Wiederaufnahme einer früheren Sitzung mithilfe von Session-Tickets. Diese Tickets enthalten das Schlüsselmaterial und müssen daher geschützt werden.Session-Tickets wurden bereits dafür kritisiert, dass sie die Forward Secrecy von TLS untergraben können. Dennoch wurden Implementierungen von Session-Tickets bislang nicht gründlich analysiert. Wir haben die Sicherheit von Session-Tickets in TLS systematisch analysiert und potenzielle Implementierungsprobleme identifiziert. Wir haben die Ticketformate von 14 Open-Source-TLS-Bibliotheken analysiert und bei fünf Bibliotheken Partitioning-Oracle-Schwachstellen gefunden. Ansonsten haben wir die Bibliotheken als sicher befunden. Dennoch haben wir festgestellt, dass bei großen HTTPS-Servern, die auf diesen Bibliotheken aufbauen, die Client-Authentifizierung durch Sitzungsaufnahme umgangen werden konnte, wenn Virtual Hosting verwendet wird. Wir haben unsere Angriffe in der Praxis evaluiert und dabei schwerwiegende Schwachstellen bei großen Cloud-Anbietern wie AWS, Cloudflare und Fastly aufgedeckt. Unsere Schwachstellen umgingen die Vertraulichkeits- und Authentifizierungsgarantien von TLS, sodass ein Angreifer die Sicherheit der Kommunikation vollständig brechen konnte. Wir vertreten die Ansicht, dass missbrauchsresistente APIs und umfassendere Leitlinien in den TLS-Standards solche Schwachstellen verhindern könnten.

title: Supervised Learning Methods
abstract: This chapter surveys a representative set of supervised learning algorithms, emphasizing intuition rather than exhaustive coverage. Using a two-predictor digit dataset that can be visualized, it compares how different methods learn decision rules from data. Readers encounter approaches such as logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, naive Bayes, linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, decision trees, and random forests. The chapter explains how algorithms differ in assumptions, flexibility, tuning parameters, and susceptibility to overfitting. By using the `caret` package, it also introduces a unified interface for fitting and comparing models. Readers learn why no single algorithm is universally best and why evaluation and context guide method choice.

title: Measure Now, Mitigate Later: Virtual Error Cancellation for Logical Quantum Circuits
abstract: Early fault-tolerant quantum algorithms are a key step in scalable quantum computing, but are ultimately constrained by residual, uncorrectable logical errors. Logical quantum error mitigation can eliminate this bias, however its standard requirements include prior noise characterization, more complex experiments, and substantial sampling overhead. Although no mitigation technique can simultaneously overcome all three constraints, we demonstrate that the first two---noise learning and need for modified circuits---can be completely bypassed for logical circuits by leveraging only syndrome records. Specifically, we introduce virtual error cancellation: a method that, unlike previous bias-free approaches, operates entirely in classical post-processing on universal quantum circuits. We develop and numerically test end-to-end protocols that reduce the sampling overhead beyond fundamental limitations of existing syndrome-aware mitigation techniques, including syndrome-based postselection. In particular, we propose a scheme that pairs the low-latency decoder used in the experiment with a high-complexity decoder run in post-processing. In numerical simulations of a distance-7 rotated surface code, we show that our full-stack dual-decoder algorithm exhibits an error that diminishes as the number of samples increases, capable of reaching more than three orders of magnitude of suppression compared to the decoded logical error rate in an experimentally achievable setting. These results establish syndrome records as a resource for correcting universal computational estimates after quantum execution.

title: Residual Modeling Closes the Regression and Generative Policy Gap in Robot Learning
abstract: Learning from demonstration has enabled impressive robot behaviors. A common choice for policy learning is to use diffusion or flow matching (Flow-Policies), which often outperforms direct action regression trained with mean squared error (MSE-Policies). This gap is commonly attributed to multimodal demonstrations. We revisit this gap from the perspective of statistical modeling: how action-prediction residuals shape policy optimization. Our analysis of real-world robot demonstration data reveals substantial state-dependent variation in residual scales and heavier-than-Gaussian tails. While both MSE-Policies and Flow-Policies exhibit heavy-tailed action residuals, their training gradients behave differently: MSE allocates more gradient magnitude to observations with large action residuals, which hurts optimization. Motivated by these findings, we introduce heteroscedastic Student-t action regression (HT-Policies), which learns input-dependent residual scales and reduces the influence of heavy tails. HT-Policies predict action chunks with a single feed-forward pass and can reuse pretrained flow-matching-based policy networks as the backbone. Across four simulation benchmarks and real-robot evaluations, HT-Policies achieves success rates competitive with generative policy baselines, both when trained from scratch and from pretrained vision-language-action and world-action models, despite being faster in training and inference. Together, these findings shed light on the practical advantages of generative objectives in robot learning from demonstrations and offer an efficient direct-regression alternative for a range of architectures and tasks. Project page: https://projects.thelabone.org/regression-policy/

title: ContourVLA: A Closed-Loop Perception-Action Contour Policy for Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation
abstract: Generalized referring expression segmentation (GRES) requires dynamically balancing high-level semantics for identifying a variable number of language-specified referents with fine-grained visual evidence for precise boundary delineation. This requirement challenges existing cascaded vision-language architectures, which typically rely on static feature interfaces and single-pass mask prediction, limiting adaptive perception and geometric correction. We introduce ContourVLA, a vision-language-action policy that recasts GRES as a closed-loop visuomotor process, in which editable contours serve as explicit policy states that condition multimodal perception and are updated by geometric action chunks. Evolution-Aware Semantic Scheduling (EASS) couples contour-guided bidirectional boundary sampling with state-conditioned routing of multilevel multimodal features, adapting perception to each contour state. Following supervised initialization, Dustbin-Augmented Entropic Credit Transport GRPO (DECT-GRPO) jointly optimizes discrete grounding and continuous contour actions with instance-level credits. Its rollout rewards and credits are derived from soft prediction-target correspondences that account for false positives and missed targets. ContourVLA improves gIoU over the strongest evaluated baselines by 8.7, 2.8, and 2.7 points on gRefCOCO val, testA, and testB, respectively, and achieves the highest mIoU across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits.

title: PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Adapting a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) road scene to a new time of day requires learning appearance changes from a few anchor images while preserving consistent, real-time rendering. We propose PAM-ToD, a lightweight plug-in that learns color corrections while keeping the pre-trained 3DGS parameters fixed. PAM-ToD scales each Gaussian's existing color to model illumination changes and uses an additive term for additional brightness, such as when street lamps turn on at night. Under a simplified image formation model, unchanged surface albedo can be eliminated from the relation between source and target appearances, allowing us to learn these corrections without separately estimating albedo and illumination. The model corrects colors across the scene while allowing the corrections to vary by location and by Gaussian. To guide learning from a few anchor images, it discourages abrupt spatial changes in these corrections. We also introduce CARLA-ToD, a benchmark with matching geometry, camera poses, and moving-object trajectories across three times of day. A few target-time anchor images are used to train each plug-in, while separate views are used for evaluation. Across the static and dynamic settings, PAM-ToD achieves higher PSNR and lower LPIPS than the baselines, even when the anchor images come from a single synchronized capture across multiple cameras.

title: Algorithmes quantiques performants de clustering de données
abstract: Data clustering consists of grouping data without prior training, a process known as unsupervised learning. Given the constant growth of database volumes, contemporary computers require significant computational time to perform this partitioning. To effectively address this challenge, quantum computing offers a promising perspective, as it could eventually provide more efficient resources for clustering massive datasets. However, current quantum computers are not yet mature; they are prone to noise, which limits their practical utility. In this context, we have designed a hybrid classical-quantum clustering algorithm tailored for the current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era. We evaluated this algorithm under various conditions and across different types of datasets, comparing it against several well-known clustering algorithms. Our results demonstrate that, under certain conditions, quantum noise can actually provide an advantage to our algorithm. Furthermore, we worked on deploying this algorithm on actual quantum processors and developed tools to optimize this deployment. Finally, to diversify the quantum architectures used, we extended our research to include neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: CQs in Ontology Engineering - Sistematic Mapping Study
abstract: The interest in the ontology subject has grown in recent decades. Ontologies can be used to assign semantics to information items and solve interoperability and knowledge-related problems. Various methods have been proposed to support ontology engineering. Several suggest using competency questions (CQs) to define the ontology requirements and help identify the necessary concepts, properties, and relations. CQs are questions the ontology must be able to answer. They establish a kind of “contract” about what the ontology must address. Aiming to investigate the use of CQs in ontology requirements engineering, we carried out a systematic mapping study. The results show that CQs have been considered useful in defining the ontology scope, but there has been a lack of specific guidelines and tools to support CQs formulation and management, which makes it difficult to write, use, and manage CQs. These findings converge with the results of a survey we conducted with 63 ontology engineers, indicating alignment between the evidence identified in the mapped literature and the state of practice in the use of CQs in ontology requirements engineering.

abstract: Implicit is the experience layer for AI agents: versioned addressing and selective state materialization with local execution evidence. इंटेलिजेंस (AI) से बिल्कुल अलग है। यह एक ऐसा स्वतन्त्र रूप से सोचने वाला कोर बाइनरी आर्किटेक्चर है, जो किसी बने-बनाए सॉफ्टवेयर लेयर पर निर्भर नहीं करता, बल्कि सीधे 0 और 1 (बाइनरी कोड) की मूलभूत शक्ति का उपयोग करके ब्रह्मांड की किसी भी जटिल समस्या का तत्काल समाधान निकाल सकता है। 2. मुख्य विशेषताएं एवं तकनीकी कार्यप्रणाली (Core Features & Working Mechanism) 🎙️ अ. प्रैक्टिकल माइक एवं बाइनरी कनवर्टर (Universal Bio-Link) यह सिस्टम एक अत्यंत संवेदनशील 'प्रैक्टिकल माइक' से लैस है। यह सिर्फ इंसानी आवाज़ ही नहीं, बल्कि प्रकृति और जीवों की सूक्ष्म तरंगों (Acoustic Frequencies) को भी कैप्चर करता है। इसका इन-बिल्ट एनालॉग-टू-बाइनरी कनवर्टर इन आवाजों को तुरंत बाइनरी डेटा में बदल देता है। इसके माध्यम से यह कंप्यूटर जानवरों की भाषाओं का सटीक इंसानी भाषा में अनुवाद करने में सक्षम है। 🧠 ब. मुख्य बाइनरी प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट (Self-Thinking Engine) यह इस कंप्यूटर का मस्तिष्क है जो पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र रूप से विचार करने (Self-Thinking Capability) में सक्षम है। यह डेटा का विश्लेषण करने के लिए किसी बाहरी एआई मॉडल का उपयोग नहीं करता, बल्कि कोर बाइनरी प्रोसेसिंग के जरिए खुद सही निर्णय लेता है। 🛠️ स. असीमित टूल लाइब्रेरी (Infinite Tool Matrix) इस कंप्यूटर के भीतर असीमित (Infinite) डिजिटल और वैज्ञानिक टूल्स का समावेश है। यह कला (पेंटिंग, संगीत, लेखन) से लेकर उन्नत विज्ञान (3D आर्किटेक्चर ढांचा, केमिकल फॉर्मूलेशन) तक सब कुछ खुद तैयार कर सकता है। 3. वैश्विक संकटों का समाधान (Universal Solution Architecture) • 2-मिनट वायरस एवं बीमारी निवारण: देश में किसी भी नए वायरस, कैंसर या महामारी के फैलने पर, यह कंप्यूटर वायरस के जेनेटिक स्ट्रक्चर को बाइनरी लेवल पर डिकोड करता है। यह मात्र 2 मिनट के भीतर शत-प्रतिशत सटीक दवा का रासायनिक फॉर्मूला और उत्पादन का ब्लूप्रिंट तैयार कर देता है। • पर्यावरण एवं आपदा प्रबंधन: भूकंप, बाढ़ या मौसम में बदलाव की सटीक भविष्यवाणी करने के साथ-साथ यह इंसानों के बचाव का लाइव रूट मैप भी तैयार करता है। पानी के संकट के दौरान, यह हवा की नमी और अणुओं को री-स्ट्रक्चर करके कृत्रिम पानी बनाने की मशीन का 3D ढांचा डिज़ाइन कर सकता है। 4. आत्मनिर्भर हाइब्रिड ऊर्जा प्रणाली (Triple-Power Sustain System) इस आविष्कार की सबसे बड़ी यूटिलिटी इसकी ऊर्जा आत्मनिर्भरता है। इसे दुनिया के किसी भी कोने में बिना बिजली ग्रिड के चलाया जा सकता है क्योंकि यह तीन प्रकार की ऊर्जा से संचालित होता है: 1. सौर ऊर्जा (Advanced Solar Cells): धूप से चार्ज होने के लिए। 2. पवन ऊर्जा (Micro-Wind Gatherers): हवा के दबाव से ऊर्जा बनाने के लिए। 3. पारंपरिक बिजली (Direct Grid): सामान्य बिजली प्लग-इन के लिए। 5. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion) आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वारा 'टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर' मानव सभ्यता को एक नए स्वर्ण युग (Golden Age) में ले जाने की क्षमता रखता है। यह एक ऐसी मशीन है जो हर क्षेत्र में असीमित समाधान देने के लिए बनाई गई है। 🌐 आधिकारिक तकनीकी लेख: टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर (Tool Point Computer) आविष्कारकर्ता (Inventor): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) श्रेणी (Category): नेक्स्ट-जेन कोर बाइनरी गुना अधिक बारीक फ्रीक्वेंसी को रिकॉर्ड करेगा, जिससे जानवरों की सबसे धीमी आवाज भी बाइनरी कोड में बदली जा सकेगी। • माइक्रो-विंड टरबाइन सेंसर्स (Piezoelectric Wind Vents): कंप्यूटर के कोनों पर छोटे वेंट्स (हवा के मार्ग) जिनमें पीजोइलेक्ट्रिक मैटेरियल लगा होगा। जब हवा इनके अंदर से गुजरेगी, तो हवा के दबाव से तुरंत बिजली पैदा होगी। 6. निष्कर्ष (Conclusion) आविष्कारकर्ता बंटी कुमावत द्वार डिज़ाइन किया गया 'टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर' मानव सभ्यता को एक नए स्वर्ण युग (Golden Age) में ले जाने की क्षमता रखता है। यह उन्नत सामग्रियों और असीमित बाइनरी टूल्स का एक ऐसा अभूतपूर्व मिश्रण है जो हर क्षेत्र में इंसानी प्रजाति को एक अचूक सुरक्षा कवच और विकास की असीमित शक्ति प्रदान करता है। टूल पॉइंट कंप्यूटर का संपूर्ण पायथन कोड # ============================================================================== # TOOL POINT COMPUTER - CORE INTEGRATED SOFTWARE SYSTEM # Inventor: Banti Kumawat # Category: Next-Gen Core Binary Computing & Universal Problem Solving Architecture # ============================================================================== import time import math import random class ToolPointComputer: def __init__(self): print("="*60) print("INITIALIZING TOOL POINT COMPUTER CORE ENGINE...") print("INVENTOR: BANTI KUMAWAT") print("="*60) time.sleep(1) # Core Hardware States (ट्रिपल पावर सिस्टम की स्थिति) self.power_sources = {"Solar": 0.0, "Wind": 0.0, "Grid": 100.0} self.is_running = True # Infinite Tool Matrix Subsystems (असीमित टूल लाइब्रेरी) self.tool_library = { "1": "Universal Animal Language Binary Decoder (जानवरों की भाषा अनुवादक)", "2": "2-Minute Global Pandemic & Virus Formula Synthesizer (2-मिनट वायरस निवारण)", "3": "3D Scientific Structural Architecture & Engineering (CAD ढांचा निर्माण)", "4": "Atmospheric Moisture Re-Structuring Water Generator (पानी बनाने का टूल)", "5": "Creative Arts Canvas (Painting, Music, Poetry)" } # 1. TRIPLE-POWER SUSTAIN SYSTEM (बिजली, धूप और हवा की ऑटो-ट्यूनिंग) def update_power_status(self, solar_input, wind_input, grid_connected=True): """Monitors and switches between the three hybrid power sources automatically.""" self.power_sources["Solar"] = max(0.0, min(100.0, solar_input)) self.power_sources["Wind"] = max(0.0, min(100.0, wind_input)) self.power_sources["Grid"] = 100.0 if grid_connected else 0.0 total_available = self.power_sources["Solar"] + self.power_sources["Wind"] + self.power_sources["Grid"] return total_available > 0 # 2. title: tidymatrix: Tidyverse-Style Operations on Matrices with Row and Column Metadata

title: Primal-Dual Flow Matching for Sample-Wise Constrained Generation
abstract: We consider the problem of learning to generate data while satisfying a prescribed \emph{sample-wise} constraint with a user-specified probability of constraint satisfaction. Starting with a population-level constrained negative log-likelihood minimization and using a flow-matching (FM) parameterization, under regularity assumptions and sufficient expressivity of the velocity field family, we derive guarantees on the probability of constraint satisfaction for the corresponding primal-dual optimization algorithm. We provide a practical implementation of this approach, called Primal-Dual Flow Matching (PDFM), which has direct control over constraint satisfaction rate and requires only binary membership oracle feedback for constraint satisfaction, avoiding the need for differentiable distances, projections, or special structure of the constraint set, such as convexity. We show that PDFM improves constraint satisfaction over vanilla FM and achieves competitive performance against constraint-aware baselines while maintaining distributional fidelity. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZhengyanHuan/PDFM.

title: Could LLM Watermark Detection be Public?
abstract: Watermarking large language models is popular for tracing chatbot and agentic outputs, yet detectors remain unreleased since exposing them could let attackers do targeted edits with the detector's feedback. However, watermarks are already vulnerable to uninformed tampering attacks. We thus first quantify whether a public detector would be an additional liability in a deployment setting at varying levels of access, from token-level scores to a binary verdict. Second, we introduce a split-key public-private watermarking method that exposes one key through a public detector while keeping the other for full verification and forensics. An informed attacker can only move the public signal, creating an imbalance between public and private scores. We introduce a statistical test for this imbalance, and combine it with the full key verdict in a two-stage mechanism. Third, we evaluate the split-key method on a wide range of removal and forgery attacks, comparing the uninformed to detector-informed settings. Public detection improves removal only at small edit budgets, since plain rephrasing already strips the watermark at a lower quality cost, but it does enable forgery, which the private pipeline can identify. Overall, releasing half of the watermark enables transparency and interoperability, and tampering with the released half stays detectable. This bounds the provider's liability and questions the need to keep detectors fully private.

title: Automated Detection of Match Phases in Football from Spatio-Temporal Tracking Data Using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Spatio-temporal tracking data has opened new possibilities for detecting complex tactical patterns in football, yet modeling the interactive movements of multiple players remains challenging. This paper proposes a framework combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with a sequential model to classify match phases on a second-by-second basis across a seven-class taxonomy. Match phase classification is tactically meaningful, and the availability of rule-based labels across 203 matches makes it a suitable testbed for a systematic comparison of adjacency constructions and message-passing layers, a question that has received limited attention in existing research. Our selected GNN-LSTM model outperforms all aggregated-feature baselines, including XGBoost and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, as the strongest baseline scores 4.6% lower in macro F1. Graph representations using a domain-informed Delaunay triangulation that approximates passing lanes, paired with a custom Spatial Edge-Augmented Convolution (SEAConv) layer that injects edge attributes directly into messages, achieve the best performance by capturing spatial dependencies while limiting uninformative messages from redundant edges. Integrated Gradients attributions indicate the model uses spatial player configurations, particularly horizontal positioning, in combination with possession and ball-status indicators. This work offers an automated solution for fine-grained tactical analysis, reducing the need for manual tagging and providing deeper insight into dynamic team behavior.

title: Defensive Writing in GPT Models
abstract: Researchers increasingly use ChatGPT to revise their papers, and when asked to make a paper hold up under review, recent GPT versions often narrow or even retract the authors' claims. We call such changes defensive writing when the given material does not support them, and we test two explanations: the model corrects the authors' overclaiming, or it writes for an anticipated reviewer. We ask GPT versions and models from other developers to rewrite paragraphs from papers written before ChatGPT, or to write from an evidence sheet that lists a paper's method and results. From GPT-5.5 on, GPT versions add clearly more ungrounded qualifications than the authors' originals contain, and GPT-6-astra adds the most and often retracts the authors' claims. Each explanation fits one part. Checked against the full papers, GPT-6-astra's retractions mostly correct overstated claims or explanations, but most added qualifications are redundant. The qualifications follow the request: they are absent under polishing, appear with any request to check the claims, and peak when the prompt names a reviewer's concerns. AI reviewers score such rewrites higher and score them lower once only the qualifications are removed, while human readers in a small study find them harder to read. Combining AI writing with AI review may reward qualifications that readers pay for.

abstract: This repository documents the foundational codebase and theoretical proofs of the Hammad OS Sovereign Architecture. This guarantees an 80% reduction in VRAM and establishes a biological-style immune system within an operating system kernel.

title: Der autonome Immobilienmanager?
abstract: Der autonome Immobilienmanager? Die Fachpublikation „Der autonome Immobilienmanager?“ untersucht die technologischen, organisatorischen, wirtschaftlichen und rechtlichen Auswirkungen Künstlicher Intelligenz auf die professionelle Immobilienbewirtschaftung. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Frage, in welchem Umfang KI-gestützte Systeme und autonome Softwareagenten Aufgaben des Property und Facility Managements übernehmen können, welche Potenziale sich daraus ergeben und wo menschliche Verantwortung, fachliche Beurteilung und organisatorische Kontrolle unverzichtbar bleiben. Ausgangspunkt ist die These, dass der eigentliche Transformationswert Künstlicher Intelligenz nicht in der isolierten Automatisierung einzelner Tätigkeiten liegt, sondern in der intelligenten Verknüpfung von Informationen, Geschäftsprozessen und operativen Handlungsschritten. Die Untersuchung differenziert zwischen regelbasierter Automatisierung, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), KI-gestützter Prozessunterstützung und agentischen Systemarchitekturen. Dabei wird aufgezeigt, wie bestehende immobilienwirtschaftliche Softwarelösungen durch KI-Funktionen und übergreifende Agentensysteme erweitert werden können. Besonderes Augenmerk gilt der Unterscheidung zwischen sprachlicher Kompetenz, fachlicher Entscheidungsfähigkeit und tatsächlicher Handlungsautonomie sowie den technischen und organisatorischen Voraussetzungen eines zuverlässigen Systemeinsatzes. Einen zentralen Schwerpunkt bildet die praxisorientierte Analyse immobilienwirtschaftlicher Geschäftsprozesse. Hierzu zählen insbesondere Kommunikations- und Dokumentenmanagement, Vorgangs- und Ticketbearbeitung, Instandhaltungskoordination, Dienstleistersteuerung, Rechnungsprüfung, Fristenüberwachung und Berichtswesen. Anhand typischer Prozessketten wird untersucht, wie KI-Agenten Informationen erfassen, Zusammenhänge erkennen, Folgehandlungen vorbereiten und definierte Arbeitsschritte innerhalb bestehender ERP-, DMS- und Kommunikationssysteme ausführen können. Besondere Aufmerksamkeit erfahren die sicherheitskritischen, datenschutzrechtlichen und haftungsrelevanten Grenzen agentischer Automatisierung. Die Publikation behandelt Berechtigungskonzepte, Informationssicherheit, Nachvollziehbarkeit automatisierter Entscheidungen, Qualitätssicherung, menschliche Freigabevorbehalte und technische Kontrollmechanismen. Risiken durch fehlerhafte Daten, Halluzinationen generativer KI, unzulässige Systemzugriffe, manipulierte Eingaben und Automation Bias werden im Zusammenhang mit betrieblichen Governance-Strukturen analysiert. Die rechtliche und normative Einordnung berücksichtigt insbesondere die europäische KI-Regulierung, datenschutzrechtliche Anforderungen sowie internationale Standards wie ISO/IEC 42001 und ISO/IEC 23894. Darauf aufbauend entwickelt die Untersuchung einen strukturierten Bewertungsansatz für die Einführung KI-gestützter Automatisierung im Immobilienmanagement. Technische Machbarkeit, Datenqualität, Integrationsaufwand, Prozessstabilität, Wirtschaftlichkeit, Risikopotenzial und organisatorische Akzeptanz werden als miteinander verbundene Entscheidungsdimensionen betrachtet. Dabei wird verdeutlicht, weshalb nicht jeder automatisierbare Prozess zugleich einen geeigneten Anwendungsfall für autonome KI-Agenten darstellt und einfachere regelbasierte Verfahren unter bestimmten Voraussetzungen wirtschaftlicher, transparenter und zuverlässiger sein können. Der integrierte Composite Case „IMMO-VERWALTUNG SUED GmbH“ überführt diese Systematik in einen realitätsnahen Modellfall einer Immobilienverwaltung mit 4.500 Verwaltungseinheiten und 28 Mitarbeitenden. Anhand typischer Verwaltungsabläufe werden Automatisierungspotenziale, organisatorische Veränderungen, technische Abhängigkeiten und Kontrollanforderungen veranschaulicht. Der modellhafte Praxisfall dient ausdrücklich der methodischen Demonstration und stellt weder eine empirische Untersuchung noch einen Nachweis tatsächlich erzielbarer Effizienzgewinne dar. Über die technische Perspektive hinaus analysiert die Publikation die Auswirkungen auf berufliche Rollenbilder, Führungsstrukturen und die zukünftige Arbeitsorganisation. Diskutiert werden insbesondere die zunehmende Bedeutung fachlicher Kontrollkompetenz, datenbasierter Steuerung, Prozessgestaltung und verantwortlicher Entscheidungsfindung sowie die Anforderungen an Qualifizierung und Veränderungsmanagement. Die Publikation verbindet immobilienwirtschaftliche Praxis, technische Systemarchitekturen, betriebswirtschaftliche Bewertungsmethoden und regulatorische Anforderungen zu einer integrierten Betrachtung der KI-gestützten Transformation des Immobilienmanagements. Prozessmodelle, Abbildungen, Tabellen und praxisorientierte Entscheidungshilfen unterstützen die Übertragung der dargestellten Methoden auf unterschiedliche Organisationsgrößen und Verwaltungskonstellationen. Die Untersuchung richtet sich an Geschäftsführungen und Führungskräfte immobilienwirtschaftlicher Unternehmen, Immobilienverwaltungen, Property- und Facility-Management-Organisationen, Bestandshalter, Asset Manager, Digitalisierungsverantwortliche sowie an Wissenschaft, Lehre und Beratung. Im Ergebnis wird deutlich, dass KI-Agenten erhebliche Potenziale zur Veränderung operativer Geschäftsprozesse eröffnen, jedoch weder automatisch eine höhere Prozessqualität noch eine wirtschaftlich sinnvolle oder rechtlich zulässige Vollautomatisierung gewährleisten. Zukunftsfähiges Immobilienmanagement entsteht vielmehr durch das kontrollierte Zusammenwirken leistungsfähiger Technologien, belastbarer Daten, klar definierter Prozesse und verantwortlicher menschlicher Entscheidungsträger.

title: contribution-kit: Reusable toolkit for attributing a modeled quantity to its contributing factors
abstract: Declarative error attribution for prediction pipelines. Failure regimes are Boolean conditions over CSV columns, tested with risk and odds ratios; crossed regimes form a factorial table whose cells are ranked by attributable burden against an analyst-chosen baseline; and an exact Shapley decomposition of the prediction formula screens its inputs, with jointly determined inputs grouped into one player.

title: Build-My-ML
abstract: BuildMyML – An Intelligent and Explainable AutoML Project Design is an AI-powered framework that simplifies the planning and design of machine learning projects. It allows users to describe their project idea in natural language and helps transform it into a structured ML project blueprint. The system combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide context-aware recommendations for problem formulation, preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, evaluation metrics, and ML workflow design. A curated machine learning knowledge base is processed through document ingestion, text chunking, embedding generation, and semantic retrieval using Supabase and pgvector, while the Gemini API is used for language understanding and recommendation generation. The proposed system aims to reduce the manual research and expertise required for ML project planning and provide users with a more systematic, explainable, and accessible way to design machine learning projects.

title: Realistic or cartoonish? The effects of digital avatar representation on tourists’ patronage intentions
abstract: With AI increasingly applied in tourism marketing, digital avatars have become key mediators between destinations and potential tourists. Yet, the persuasive effectiveness of different avatar representations across tourism contexts remains underexplored. Drawing on processing fluency and cognitive–affective system theories, this study conducted three scenario-based experiments to examine the matching effects of avatar representation and attraction type, and their underlying psychological mechanisms. Results reveal a significant interaction: cartoonish avatars boost tourists’ patronage intentions in natural attractions, whereas realistic avatars are more effective in cultural attractions. Mediation analysis shows affection drives the effect in natural attractions, while cognitive processing is the key pathway in cultural attractions. Fantasy proneness and perceived eeriness act as critical boundary conditions. The study advances understanding of digital avatar marketing by highlighting context-dependent, dual-pathway mechanisms and the moderating role of individual differences, offering theoretical insights and practical guidance for AI-driven tourism marketing.

title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.
